correctness.rationale: The given Zak transform has an affine real numerator A−Bz divided by (1−uz)(1−vz), with correct critical-lattice lower-frame scaling alpha essinf|Z|². After y=cos angle, numerator minus a candidate endpoint minimum times denominator is concave in y, so an interior angular fiber cannot lower the minimum. On the protected interval L<R<H, one frequency endpoint branch rises, another is unimodal with minimum at an endpoint; its third candidate is globally dominated by the rising branch. This proves exact piecewise-quadratic A_R and unique balance R*. Independent parameters u=4/5,v=1/5 give L=8/3,H=4,R*=196/51, with grid of 5151 Zak fibers above predicted bound. Numerical sampling alone cannot prove the global result.
residual_risks: Check endpoint Zak values as one-sided essential limits; discontinuity between endpoints is not a frame-zero exception.
